study.title: Effects of acupuncture at the Taichong (LIV3) and Hegu (LI4) points on functional connectivity with the retrosplenial cortex in patients with Alzheimer's disease
study.study_design: Resting-state fMRI study with pre- and post-acupuncture scans in AD patients and normal controls, plus a separate dataset of 100 healthy participants for RSC connectivity mapping
study.population: 14 patients with Alzheimer's disease and 14 age-, sex-, and education-matched normal controls; plus 100 healthy participants (separate dataset for RSC connectivity mapping)
study.inclusion_criteria: AD participants: individuals who had consulted a memory clinic at Xuanwu Hospital with memory complaints; diagnosis of AD based on the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders-Fifth Edition criteria for Alzheimer's Dementia and the National Institutes on Aging and the Alzheimer's Association on diagnostic guidelines for AD. NCs: no history of neurological disease or cognitive dysfunction. Healthy participants (100): cognitive health without memory complaints and a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 28 or higher.
study.exclusion_criteria: For all participants: (1) cognitive impairment caused by head trauma or cranial surgery; (2) a history of neurological or psychiatric disorders that could cause cognitive impairments; (3) contraindications to MRI. For healthy participants (100): history of head trauma or cranial surgery, history of neurological or psychiatric disorders, or any contraindications to magnetic resonance image (MRI).
study.notes: The acupuncture group dataset is from a previously published study (Wang et al., 2014). Twenty-eight right-handed subjects participated; one AD patient was excluded due to head motion, leaving 13 AD and 14 NC for neuroimaging analyses.

arms.dropouts: 1 AD patient excluded due to head motion (poor image quality)

interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: LIV3 and LI4 are collectively known as Si Guan (The Four Gates) or Four Bars, which are thought to promote the circulation of Qi and blood throughout the body and have a calming effect. Source points (Yuan points) refer to the places where the Yuan Qi resides, surfaces, and lingers, which are hubs for internal and external energies gathering and transforming.

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: Acupuncture group: Siemens Verio 3-Tesla scanner (Siemens, Erlangen, Germany); Healthy 100 dataset: MAGNETOM Prisma 3 T MR scanner (Siemens Medical Solutions, Erlangen, Germany) with a 64-channel head-neck coil
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: Acupuncture group: gradient-echo echo-planar imaging (EPI) sequence; Healthy 100 dataset: simultaneous multislice echoplanar imaging sequence; T1: 3D MPRAGE for both datasets
neuroimaging_methods.TR_exact: Acupuncture group: TR = 3,000 ms; Healthy 100 dataset: TR = 2,000 ms
neuroimaging_methods.TE_exact: Acupuncture group: TE = 30 ms; Healthy 100 dataset: TE = 30 ms
neuroimaging_methods.voxel_size_exact: Acupuncture group: not explicitly stated for functional; Healthy 100 dataset: voxel size = 2 × 2 × 2 mm3
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: Acupuncture group: baseline 3 min resting-state; post-acupuncture 10 min resting-state; Healthy 100 dataset: not_reported
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM 12, University College London, London, United Kingdom) and the CONN-fMRI functional connectivity toolbox v22a
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: SPM 12 and CONN-fMRI functional connectivity toolbox v22a
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel of 6 × 6 × 6 mm3 full width at half maximum (FWHM)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: images with head motion exceeding 2.5 mm in any direction or 2.5° rotational movement were excluded from further analysis (one case of AD was excluded for this reason)
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: bandpass filter (below 0.008 Hz or above 0.09 Hz) followed by linear detrending
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: not_reported; noise components from cerebral WM and cerebrospinal areas were estimated and regressed out using aCompCor; estimated subject-motion parameters and identified outlier scans were also regressed out
statistical_thresholds_exact: cluster level of p < 0.05, corrected for multiple comparisons by using familywise error (FWE) [for 100 healthy participants RSC connectivity maps]

neuroimaging_methods.multiple_comparison_correction_exact: familywise error (FWE) correction for RSC connectivity maps in 100 healthy participants; Gaussian random field (GRF) theory for cluster-level multiple comparison correction in interaction effect analysis (voxel p < 0.005; cluster p < 0.05)

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture or placebo control condition was included in the acupuncture group. The authors acknowledge this as a limitation: 'It would be beneficial to include a placebo control on real-needle acupuncture by using sham acupuncture, such as nonpenetrating needling, shallow needling on nonpoints, or regular needling on nonpoints.'
Sensory/deqi responses were not measured or reported for any acupuncture condition. There is no deqi, needle sensation, or MASS scale data in this paper.
Expectancy, credibility, blinding success, and allocation guessing measures were not assessed or reported.
Adverse events were not reported. The paper does not include an adverse events section.
Trial registration number is not reported anywhere in the paper.

The acupuncture group dataset is stated to be 'from a previously published study (Wang et al., 2014).' This means the acupuncture intervention data were originally collected for a different publication, which may affect interpretation of sample size and representativeness.

The n_analyzed for the neuroimaging analyses of the acupuncture group is stated to be 27 (after excluding 1 AD patient due to head motion), comprising 13 AD and 14 NC. However, the Table 1 note states '(AD = 1)' was excluded, and the text says 'one AD patient was excluded.' The statistical analyses appear to use n = 27 total but this is not consistently stated for all analyses.

The paper does not specify whether the coordinate space for the acupuncture group data (from the 2014 dataset) and the healthy 100 dataset are both MNI. The healthy 100 dataset acquisition specifies normalization to standard MNI space. The older dataset's coordinate space is reported as MNI based on the methods description but there is no explicit confirmation in the table.

The Table 2 header labels 'F/T value' without always distinguishing which statistic was used for each row. Interaction effects appear to have F values and post hoc comparisons appear to have T values; this was inferred from context and table formatting but was used in the extraction above.

For the RSC_7mm analysis, the bilateral OFC result (Table 2) lists comparison as 'Pre_NC < Post_NC' with T = 3.70. However, the text states this was part of the interaction effect cluster. The table appears to report only the directional sub-comparison for the OFC rather than an F value for the interaction, possibly because OFC showed only the NC-specific effect. This inconsistency is preserved as reported in Table 2.

The left lingual gyrus (LG) in Table 2 for RSC_L is labeled 'Main effect' with F = 13.58, not as an interaction effect or post hoc comparison. This finding is extracted as a separate contrast (nc_007) but its interpretation in the context of the paper's main hypothesis is unclear.

The paper's text states that 'decreased FC between the left RSC and left lingual gyrus was identified only in the NC group' but Table 2 labels this row as 'Main effect.' This is an inconsistency between the text and table. The table value is used for extraction.

The n_analyzed for correlation analyses (nc_019 to nc_023) is inferred to be 13 (AD group after exclusion of 1 subject for head motion) rather than 14. The paper's text does not explicitly state n = 13 for these correlations but it does state one AD patient was excluded from neuroimaging analyses.

Functional image acquisition parameters for the acupuncture group (from Wang et al., 2014 dataset) include TR = 3,000 ms, TE = 30 ms, FA = 90°, matrix size = 64 × 64, FOV = 224 × 224 mm, ST = 3 mm, gap = 0.48 mm, 43 slices — but exact voxel size and total scan duration in volumes are not reported for this dataset.
The paper does not specify needle type, needle gauge, needle depth, or specific needle manipulation technique (e.g., lifting-thrusting, rotating) for the acupuncture intervention.

Figures 3, 4, 5, and 6 contain bar plots with individual data points showing mean FC z scores for AD and NC groups at Pre and Post conditions. The exact mean values and standard deviations from these bar plots were not extractable from the PDF with sufficient precision and are therefore not reported as exact values in the clinical_behavioral_outcomes. The significance markers (*, **, ***) are preserved in the contrast descriptions.

The healthy 100 participant dataset and the acupuncture group dataset were acquired on different scanners (MAGNETOM Prisma 3T vs. Siemens Verio 3T) and used different acquisition parameters. The healthy dataset was used only to generate RSC connectivity masks; no acupuncture intervention was performed in this group.
